module_title: Important Stadiums - Global Capacity Anomalies, Altitudes, and Niche Trivia
introduction: This advanced module addresses nuanced topics, including technical capacity disputes, stadiums located at high altitudes, and giant American or North Korean arenas that create frequent sorting traps in competitive exams.

core_concepts.title: The Rungrado 1st of May Stadium Phenomenon
core_concepts.description: Located in Pyongyang, North Korea, this multi-purpose stadium claims an absolute seating capacity of roughly 1,14,000 to 1,50,000. It is often cited as the largest stadium in the world by non-sport specific metrics, primarily used for mass gymnastics and Arirang festivals.

core_concepts.title: The American 'Big Houses'
core_concepts.description: Michigan Stadium (nicknamed 'The Big House') in the USA boasts an official capacity of over 1,07,000. It is a prime example of massive American College Football stadiums that outsize most professional soccer arenas.

core_concepts.title: The Technical Capacity Dispute Trap
core_concepts.description: If a question specifies 'Largest Cricket Stadium' or 'Largest Purpose-Built All-Seater Stadium', Narendra Modi Stadium (1.32 lakh) is the undisputed answer. If the question broadly asks for 'Largest Stadium' without sport filters and includes 'Rungrado 1st of May' in options, select the North Korean stadium.

core_concepts.title: High-Altitude Architectural Marvels
core_concepts.description: The HPCA Stadium in Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh) sits at an altitude of 1,457 meters above sea level, making it one of the highest and most scenic cricket grounds. Similarly, the Bhaichung Bhutia Football Stadium in Namchi (Sikkim) is a premier high-altitude football venue.

core_concepts.title: Disambiguating Regional Historical Grounds
core_concepts.description: Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium is located in Hyderabad, whereas Green Park Stadium—one of India's oldest traditional Test venues featuring a legacy 'Student Gallery'—is situated in Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh.

important_entities.name: Rungrado 1st of May Stadium
important_entities.significance: The largest multi-purpose stadium by absolute structural capacity globally.

important_entities.name: HPCA Stadium
important_entities.significance: High-altitude stadium famous for its fast-bowling friendly thin air and snow-capped Dhauladhar backdrop.

important_entities.name: Green Park Stadium
important_entities.significance: Located near the river Ganga; historically famous for iconic spin-friendly test tracks.

important_entities.name: Stade Roland Garros
important_entities.significance: The ultimate global cathedral for Clay Court tennis, home to the French Open.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not rush when you see 'Rajiv Gandhi Stadium'. The 'Rajiv Gandhi International Cricket Stadium' is in Hyderabad (Telangana), but the 'Rajiv Gandhi Indoor Stadium' is located in Kochi (Kerala).

Read the question's precise phrasing. If it asks for the largest stadium *overall*, check if North Korea's Rungrado is listed. Do not blindly tick Narendra Modi Stadium unless 'Cricket' or 'All-Seater sport' is explicitly contexted.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Instantly link the famous sports nickname 'The Big House' to Michigan Stadium, USA.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Cricket in Dharamshala, Football with Bhaichung
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Associate HPCA with high-altitude cricket in Dharamshala, and Bhaichung Bhutia's namesake stadium with high-altitude football in Namchi, Sikkim.

exam_strategy_tips: In advanced papers like UPSC or State PCS, questions focus heavily on unique stadium attributes (e.g., eco-friendly solar-powered venues, high altitudes, or architectural quirks).
Keep a close eye on stadium nicknames ('The Big House', 'Mecca of Cricket', 'Chepauk') as they are highly favored tools for checking deep conceptual retention.
